question_text: If f(x) = log(tan eˣ), find f′(x).

The answer was checked numerically before it was written: the central difference quotient reads 2.1995003 at x = 0 and 3.7973654 at x = 0.2; eˣsec²(eˣ)/tan(eˣ) gives 2.1995003 and 3.7973654 at the same two points, and the tidied form 2eˣ·Cosec(2eˣ) gives the identical pair, so both printed forms are the same number.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the three layers in order and say what each one contributes.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate the outer log
steps.margin_note: First mark. Three layers: log outside, tan next, eˣ innermost. The log contributes 1/(tan eˣ) and nothing else on this line.
steps.memory_tip: Whatever sits inside the log becomes the denominator, written out exactly as it stands — here that is tan eˣ.
lines: f(x) = log(tan eˣ), where log is the natural logarithm.
There are three layers: log outside, tan next, eˣ inside.
Take u = tan eˣ. Then d/dx(log u) = (1/u) · du/dx

recall.must_convey: That log is the outermost layer, so f′(x) = (1/tan eˣ) times the derivative of tan eˣ.
accept: log u gives one over u times du by dx
tan e power x goes to the denominator
there are three layers, log then tan then e power x
log lo unnadi kinda vasthundi, tan e power x
start with one over tan e power x

steps.why: Naming the layers in order fixes the shape of the answer before any derivative is computed. Doing the eˣ first is the usual way the tan layer is then forgotten.
common_mistakes: Writing the denominator as tan x instead of tan eˣ.
Writing 1/(tan eˣ) alone, with no further derivative attached.

steps.label: Differentiate tan eˣ and finish
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Two pieces sit here: tan gives sec²(eˣ), and the innermost eˣ gives eˣ again. Both forms of the final answer are accepted.
steps.memory_tip: eˣ is its own derivative, so the innermost layer appears again as a multiplying factor.
lines: This may be tidied, since sec²θ/tan θ = 1/(sin θ cos θ) = 2/sin 2θ

recall.must_convey: That d/dx(tan eˣ) = eˣsec²(eˣ), giving f′(x) = eˣsec²(eˣ)/tan(eˣ).
accept: tan gives sec squared and e power x gives e power x again
the answer is e power x sec squared e power x over tan e power x
it can also be written as two e power x cosec two e power x
tan ki sec square, e power x ki e power x ne
multiply by e power x sec squared e power x

steps.why: The first form is the direct result of the chain rule and is a complete answer on its own. The second form is shorter and shows the sec²θ/tan θ identity, so either is worth full marks.
common_mistakes: Writing d/dx(tan eˣ) = sec²(eˣ) and losing the eˣ factor.
Writing sec²x rather than sec²(eˣ), which changes the function.
